extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Congress and the American public / policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report of President Roosevelt’s special defense message to Congress, summarizing his assessment of modern defense needs and the specific appropriations and authorizations he requested. The page presents policy prescriptions, justifications, and numerical funding proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense must be dynamic and flexible
rubrics_metrics.description: Defense cannot be static. Defense must grow and change from day to day. Defense must be dynamic and flexible, an expression of the vital forces of the nation and of its resolute will to meet whatever challenge the future may hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roosevelt stresses ongoing adaptation: defenses that were adequate yesterday (or today) may not protect against future developments; Congress may be called into special session if national defense requires it; defense requires continuous growth and change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destroy enemy lines of supply and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: A defense which makes no effective effort to destroy the lines of supplies and communications of the enemy will lose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective defense by its very nature requires the equipment to attack an aggressor on his route before he can establish strong bases within the territory of American vital interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep defenses informed by lessons of actual combat
rubrics_metrics.description: Since Sept. 1, 1939, every week has brought new lessons learned from actual combat on land and sea; defenses should be updated accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: naval ships operating without defending aircraft were vulnerable to air attack; the rapid countering of a new magnetic mine demonstrates the need to incorporate combat lessons quickly into defensive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase anti-aircraft and air-defense protection
rubrics_metrics.description: All nations need additional anti-aircraft protection as naval and other forces are vulnerable without adequate defending aircraft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes increased vulnerability of ships without air protection and recommends study and investment in additional anti-aircraft defenses and defending aircraft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand aircraft production capacity (target 50,000/year and 50,000 planes total)
rubrics_metrics.description: Superimpose on existing capacity a greatly increased additional production capacity; aim to be able to turn out at least 50,000 planes a year and plan a program to provide 50,000 military and naval planes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. production had risen from ~6,000 planes/year to more than double due largely to foreign orders; foreign orders should not be impeded because they have helped expand capacity; the goal is both an annual output target and an overall procurement program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not hamper delivery of American-made planes to foreign nations
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress should not take any action which would in any way hamper or delay the delivery of American-made planes to foreign nations which have ordered them or seek to purchase more planes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roosevelt argues that foreign orders have been a major factor increasing U.S. production capacity and that obstructing such orders would be short-sighted from the standpoint of national defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate appropriation and specific funding breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Request an immediate appropriation of $896,000,000 divided approximately: $546,060,000 for the army; $250,000,000 for the navy and Marine Corps; $100,000,000 to the President for emergencies affecting national security and defense. Additionally request authorizations for contract obligations ($186,000,000) and presidential contract authorization ($100,000,000), total authorizations $286,000,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article provides precise dollar amounts and notes that these estimates do not duplicate items in pending appropriation bills and may be supplemented by further estimates as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four primary purposes for requested appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requested funds are for four primary purposes: (1) to procure the essential equipment of all kinds for a larger, thoroughly rounded-out army; (2) to replace or modernize all old army and navy equipment with the latest type of equipment; (3) to increase production facilities for everything needed for the army and navy for national defense; (4) to speed up to a twenty-four-hour basis all existing army and navy contracts and all new contracts to be awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roosevelt emphasizes immediate fulfillment rather than spreading procurements over several years, and highlights both materiel procurement and production-scale increases as priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed immediate procurement for ground forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground forces require the immediate speeding up of programs to procure equipment of all kinds, including motor transport, artillery, anti-aircraft guns and full ammunition supplies; items planned to be spread over three or four years should be filled at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administration asks Congress for urgent funding to accelerate procurement that had previously been scheduled over multiple years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production facilities must be ready to turn out munitions and equipment at top speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities for production must be ready to turn out munitions and equipment at top speed; the nation must have the ability to turn out quickly infinitely greater supplies when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supports the demand for increased production capacity and for investment in industrial readiness so that munitions and equipment can be manufactured rapidly in wartime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense readiness requires trained, morally and physically strong personnel and leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Our security is not a matter of weapons alone. The arm that wields them must be strong, the eye that guides them clear, the will that directs them indomitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roosevelt underlines that equipment must be matched by capable officers and men, and by national toughness of moral and physical fiber; readiness includes personnel quality and resolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use foreign and territorial strategic realities to shape defense posture
rubrics_metrics.description: Because modern air navigation shrinks distances, islands and bases in the Atlantic, Pacific and near Americas can be within hours of attack; strategic positioning and readiness must account for these new geographic realities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists flight-times (e.g., from Greenland to New England, Azores to eastern seaboard, Pacific islands to South America) to justify the need for mobility, forward bases, and rapid response capabilities.
